nodes.label: Qwen-AgentWorld: Language World Models for General Agents
nodes.author: Yuxin Zuo, Zikai Xiao, Li Sheng, Fei Huang, Jianhong Tu, Yuxuan Liu, Tianyi Tang, Xiaomeng Hu, Yang Su, Qingfeng Lan, Yantao Liu, Qin Zhu, Yinger Zhang, Bowen Yu, Haiquan Zhao, Haiyang Xu, Jianxin Yang, Jiayang Cheng, Junyang Wang, Lianghao Deng, Mingfeng Xue, Tianyi Bai, Yang Fan, Yubo Ma, Yucheng Li, Zeyu Cui, Zhihai Wang, Zhihui Xie, Zhuorui Ye, An Yang, Dayiheng Liu, Jingren Zhou, Ning Ding
nodes.rationale: Develops language world models for agentic environment simulation across 7 domains; demonstrates world modeling as foundation for general agents through decoupled simulator and unified agent paradigms.

nodes.label: Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B Model
nodes.rationale: Language world model trained via three-stage pipeline (CPT, SFT, RL) for simulating 7 agent interaction domains; demonstrates world modeling improves downstream agent performance.

nodes.label: Qwen-AgentWorld-397B-A17B Model
nodes.rationale: Larger language world model achieving highest overall score on AgentWorldBench; demonstrates scalability of world modeling approach across text and GUI domains.

nodes.label: AgentWorldBench: Comprehensive World Model Evaluation Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Benchmark constructed from frontier model trajectories on 9 established benchmarks across 7 domains; evaluates simulation quality through 5-dimensional rubric (Format, Factuality, Consistency, Realism, Quality) with reference-grounded judging.

nodes.label: Language World Model (LWM) Concept
nodes.rationale: Conditional text generator predicting next environment observation given interaction history and agent action; enables both environment simulation and agent foundation model training.

nodes.label: Unified Environment Trajectory Schema
nodes.rationale: Shared format across 7 domains comprising system prompt (task description, action space, initial state, demonstrations, simulation instruction) and alternating (action, observation) turns; enables cross-domain training.

nodes.label: Three-Stage Training Pipeline: CPT → SFT → RL
nodes.rationale: CPT injects world knowledge from trajectories and domain corpora; SFT activates explicit next-state-prediction reasoning; RL sharpens fidelity with hybrid rubric-and-rule rewards.

nodes.label: Decoupled Environment Simulator Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Uses LWM as standalone environment simulator for agentic RL; provides scalability (4k environments without infrastructure) and controllability (targeted perturbations) beyond real environments.

nodes.label: Unified Agent Foundation Model Paradigm
nodes.rationale: World-model training serves as warm-up for downstream agent tasks; internalizes next-state prediction as meta-level thinking pattern improving agent decision-making across 7 benchmarks.

nodes.label: Continual Pre-Training Stage
nodes.rationale: Injects world knowledge through next-token prediction on environment trajectories and specialized-domain corpora; uses turn-level information-theoretic loss masking to focus on genuine environment information.

nodes.label: Supervised Fine-Tuning Stage
nodes.rationale: Activates explicit next-state-prediction reasoning patterns; uses rejection sampling to curate high-quality trajectories; diversifies prompt templates to improve generalization.

nodes.label: Reinforcement Learning Stage
nodes.rationale: Sharpens simulation fidelity using GSPO with hybrid rubric-and-rule rewards; addresses reward collapse, reward shaping, and reward hacking through systematic design choices.

nodes.label: Turn-Level Information-Theoretic Loss Masking
nodes.rationale: Categorizes turns into 7 semantic categories (retrieval, expansion, action, transform, boilerplate, echo, other) based on statistical signals; masks low-information turns to focus learning on genuine environment knowledge.

nodes.label: Five-Dimensional Evaluation Rubric
nodes.rationale: Evaluates Format (structural compliance), Factuality (correctness of facts), Consistency (internal and cross-turn coherence), Realism (behavioral match to real environment), Quality (completeness and conciseness).

nodes.label: Reference-Grounded Judging Protocol
nodes.rationale: Judge receives ground-truth observation alongside prediction; converts evaluation from open-ended quality judgment to factual comparison; substantially reduces judge hallucination and improves cross-judge consistency.

nodes.label: Domain-Aware Rubric Customization
nodes.rationale: Each domain has tailored judge prompt applying five dimensions in domain-specific terms; enforces professional standards (shell prompts for Terminal, JSON schema for MCP, fact-priority for Search).

nodes.label: Differentiated Matching Criteria
nodes.rationale: Classifies content into deterministic (exact match required), pre-existing (format/plausibility only), runtime metadata (format/range only); reduces false negatives from irreproducible details.

nodes.label: Seven Agent Interaction Domains
nodes.rationale: MCP (tool calls), Search (web queries), Terminal (bash commands), SWE (code editing), Android (UI navigation), Web (browser interaction), OS (desktop interaction); unified under single language world model.

nodes.label: Scalable Environment Generation
nodes.rationale: LWM enables turn-level scaling of diverse environments without dedicated infrastructure; simulates 4k OpenClaw environments for agentic RL entirely absent from training.

nodes.label: Controllable Simulation Capability
nodes.rationale: LWM offers precise controllability enabling targeted perturbations (partial results, resource constraints) that expose agent weaknesses rare in real environments; surpasses real-environment training alone.

nodes.label: Cross-Domain Generalization in World Modeling
nodes.rationale: Training RL on Terminal alone improves all text domains (SWE +11.5, Search +11.8, MCP +5.0); suggests learning generalizable world knowledge rather than domain-specific behaviors.

nodes.label: AutoML-Based System Prompt Optimization
nodes.rationale: Formulates prompt optimization as automated research problem; iterative propose-evaluate-refine cycles with optimizer and judge agents; generates 12 template variants with different styles.

nodes.label: Trajectory-to-Turn Expansion Technique
nodes.rationale: Expands multi-turn trajectories into turn-level prediction samples; any turn can serve as prediction target with preceding interactions as input; diversifies training objectives.

nodes.label: Retry-Cycle Skipping Data Filter
nodes.rationale: Skips garbage-output-error-retry cycles while preserving state chain; prevents breaking causal relationships between actions and observations.

nodes.label: No-Change Turn Filtering for GUI Domains
nodes.rationale: Removes turns where pre-action and post-action states show no effective change; prevents teaching model to copy previous state regardless of action.

nodes.label: Reward Collapse Mitigation Strategy
nodes.rationale: Restricts trajectory expansion to exactly one turn per trajectory in RL pool; prevents shared-prefix overlap causing reward variance collapse and policy degeneration.

nodes.label: Reward Hacking Prevention Mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Combines rule-based verifier (binary anchor), content-type classification (deterministic content exact match), and tag extraction (separates thinking from prediction) to prevent self-praise exploitation.

nodes.label: Hybrid Rubric-and-Rule Reward Design
nodes.rationale: Combines 5-dimensional LLM rubric (multi-dimensional feedback) with rule-based verifier (binary correctness); 9:1 weighting balances open-ended feedback with objective anchor.

nodes.label: GSPO Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Used for RL stage; handles extreme prompt-output asymmetry in LWM training; caps prompt at 128k tokens for computational efficiency.

nodes.label: Turing Test Calibration for Judge Selection
nodes.rationale: Uses double-blind Turing test to select judge model and tune prompts; judge with high Turing-test accuracy must attend to fine-grained differences between faithful and plausible-but-wrong simulation.

nodes.label: Cross-Judge Consistency Analysis
nodes.rationale: Compares three frontier models as judges; achieves Spearman rank correlations ρ=0.92-0.99; reference-grounded design enables high consistency despite absolute score differences.

nodes.label: LWM Reasoning Patterns Analysis
nodes.rationale: Analyzes how LWM engages in reasoning; demonstrates next-state prediction requires reasoning, knowledge, instruction following, long-context handling—foundational to general agents.

nodes.label: RL Enhancement of Micro-Level Simulation Fidelity
nodes.rationale: RL training improves simulation fidelity at fine-grained level; different rubric dimensions improve at markedly different rates; Factuality shows largest relative improvement yet remains lowest-scoring.

nodes.label: World Modeling as Agent Foundation
nodes.rationale: LWM training serves as warm-up for downstream agent tasks; improves performance across 7 benchmarks; internalizes next-state prediction as meta-level thinking pattern.

nodes.label: Fictional Worlds Generalization Capability
nodes.rationale: Agents trained in fully invented, self-consistent simulated worlds generalize to real tasks; prevents agent from confusing simulated facts with real-world knowledge.

nodes.label: Initial State as Critical Bottleneck
nodes.rationale: Sim RL effectiveness depends on sufficiently detailed initial state; without it, simulation fidelity degrades and downstream gains diminish.

nodes.label: Environment Trajectory Collection Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Combines dedicated agent infrastructure, open environment interaction traces, and in-house agentic trajectories; multi-agent cleaning pipeline handles fetching, denoising, segmentation, semantic alignment.

nodes.label: Accessibility Tree Representation for GUI
nodes.rationale: GUI observations represented as accessibility trees and UI view hierarchies rather than pixel frames; enables text-based world modeling for Android, Web, OS domains.

nodes.label: Stateless vs Stateful Environment Distinction
nodes.rationale: Stateless environments (Search) carry state implicitly in conversation history; stateful environments (Terminal, OS) maintain explicit internal state; LWM operates uniformly over both.

nodes.label: Qwen-AgentWorld: Language World Models for Agent Training
nodes.author: Yuxin Zuo, Zikai Xiao, Li Sheng, Fei Huang, Jianhong Tu
nodes.rationale: Language world models trained via CPT→SFT→RL pipeline to simulate diverse agent environments across 7 domains, enabling both decoupled Sim RL and unified agent foundation models.

nodes.label: AgentWorldBench: LWM Evaluation Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Benchmark pairing every sample with ground-truth observation from real environments, evaluating LWM across five dimensions: Format, Factuality, Consistency, Realism, Quality.

nodes.label: Sim RL: Simulated Reinforcement Learning
nodes.rationale: Training agents in simulated environments generated by LWM, with controllable simulation instructions to inject targeted perturbations and improve agent robustness.

nodes.label: Controllable Simulation: Environment Adaptation & Fictional-World Construction
nodes.rationale: Two complementary modes: (1) Environment Adaptation injects targeted perturbations via natural-language instructions; (2) Fictional-World Construction generates self-consistent fictional environments for search agents.

nodes.label: LWM RL Warm-up: Agent Foundation Model
nodes.rationale: Single-turn LWM RL on next-state prediction transfers to multi-turn tool-calling agentic tasks across seven benchmarks, demonstrating radical cross-task and domain generalization.

nodes.label: Mental Simulation: Prediction-Driven Action Refinement
nodes.rationale: LWM-trained agents systematically perform mental simulation of environment responses before executing actions, using internalized world model to predict outcomes and refine action plans.

nodes.label: LWM Reasoning Patterns: Deliberative Self-Correction, Information Leakage Prevention, Multi-Step Causal Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Three representative reasoning patterns: (1) Deliberative Self-Correction uses 'Wait!' interrupts to revise predictions; (2) Information Leakage Prevention distinguishes agent knowledge from environment revelation; (3) Multi-Step Causal Reasoning chains across system abstractions.

nodes.label: Micro-Level Fidelity Improvements: URL Realism, Byte Arithmetic, API Schema Consistency
nodes.rationale: RL training improves fidelity at fine granularity: URL identifiers, character-level byte arithmetic, cross-turn API schema consistency maintained across multiple sequential calls.

nodes.label: OpenClaw: Out-of-Distribution Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Open-source real-world AI agent platform with tasks from real user multi-step digital workflows (scheduling, coding, email, browser automation, file management), entirely out-of-distribution for testing generalization.

nodes.label: Three-Stage Training Pipeline: CPT→SFT→RL
nodes.rationale: Progressive training: CPT injects environment knowledge, SFT activates next-state-prediction reasoning, RL sharpens simulation fidelity across seven domains.

nodes.label: Seven Agent Interaction Domains
nodes.rationale: Terminal, MCP Tool Use, Search, Software Engineering, Android, Web, OS—covering text-based and GUI-based agent environments.

nodes.label: World-Model–Actor Unification Architecture
nodes.rationale: Same model serves as both agent (action selection) and world model (environment state prediction), aligning with LeCun et al. (2022) vision and World Action Model paradigm.

nodes.label: Claw-Eval & QwenClawBench: Out-of-Domain Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Real-world digital workflow benchmarks entirely absent from LWM training; Sim RL with Qwen-AgentWorld-397B-A17B improves Claw-Eval +4.3 and QwenClawBench +7.1 over base model.

nodes.label: Tool Decathlon & MCPMark: MCP Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Tool Decathlon covers 32 software applications; MCPMark evaluates 127 multi-step tasks; controllable Sim RL improves Tool Decathlon +3.7 and MCPMark +12.3 over uncontrolled baseline.

nodes.label: WideSearch: Fictional-World Search Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 200 manually curated information-seeking tasks; agents trained entirely in fictional environments generalize to real-world search; Qwen3.5-35B-A3B improves F1 Item +16.29, F1 Row +10.49.

nodes.label: Terminal-Bench 2.0: Terminal Agent Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Hard, realistic terminal tasks; LWM RL warm-up improves accuracy +6.30 on single-turn next-state prediction, transferring to multi-turn tool-calling agentic tasks.

nodes.label: SWE-Bench Verified & Pro: Software Engineering Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Real GitHub issues; LWM RL improves SWE-Bench Verified +3.39 and SWE-Bench Pro +5.24 resolve rate, demonstrating transfer from single-turn to multi-turn software engineering tasks.

nodes.label: BFCL v4: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard
nodes.rationale: Out-of-domain function-calling benchmark; LWM RL improves +9.0 on BFCL v4, confirming transferable agent capabilities rather than domain-specific shortcuts.

nodes.label: Environment Prediction Accuracy Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures fraction of correctly predicted environment responses in thinking traces; LWM RL improves from 69.9% to 78.3% (+8.4%), confirming internal world model becomes more faithful.

nodes.label: Rule-Based Verification: Controllability, Error Handling, Long-Context Consistency
nodes.rationale: Three deterministic verification axes: (1) Controllability (adherence to simulation instructions), (2) Error Handling (faithful error reproduction), (3) Long-Context Consistency (coherent state tracking).

nodes.label: Open-Ended Rubric Evaluation: Five Dimensions
nodes.rationale: Five evaluation dimensions applied across all domains: Format (structural adherence), Factuality (correctness), Consistency (coherence with prior state), Realism (authentic behavior), Quality (completeness/conciseness).

nodes.label: Training Dynamics: Per-Dimension Improvement Rates
nodes.rationale: Format converges within ~90 steps; Consistency requires ~250 steps; Factuality improves most in relative terms (+11.3%) but remains lowest-scoring dimension throughout training.

nodes.label: Qwen Model Variants: 35B-A3B and 397B-A17B
nodes.rationale: Two scales of Qwen-AgentWorld: 35B-A3B (smaller, faster) and 397B-A17B (larger, more capable); both trained via CPT→SFT→RL pipeline across seven domains.

nodes.label: Baseline Comparisons: Qwen3.6-Plus, GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6
nodes.rationale: Qwen-AgentWorld-397B-A17B competitive with frontier models; rule-based verification shows GPT-5.4 ranks first (72.93 avg), Qwen-AgentWorld-397B-A17B second (67.12), outperforming on GUI domains.

nodes.label: Real RL vs. Sim RL Comparison
nodes.rationale: Controllable Sim RL tracks or exceeds Real RL on WideSearch; Sim RL increases web_extractor calls (2.5→4.0) while Real RL decreases (2.5→1.5), reflecting deliberate information withholding in simulation.

nodes.label: Case Study: Mailman Task - Prediction-Driven Action Refinement
nodes.rationale: Before LWM RL: incorrect prediction of Postfix processing order leads to futile exploration. After LWM RL: correct prediction enables targeted fix to local_recipient_maps, demonstrating mental simulation enabling action refinement.

edges.rationale: Both represent AI systems as epistemic actors capable of reasoning and planning; LWM is technical instantiation of reasoning capability needed for AI scientists.
Multi-agent systems coordinate specialized agents; LWM provides world knowledge enabling coordination; both enable reasoning beyond single-model capabilities.

Both papers address persistent data management for LLM agents; Qwen-AgentWorld focuses on environment simulation while agent memory focuses on information storage/retrieval, but both are foundational infrastructure for agent execution.
Both address unified agent architectures; world-model–actor unification parallels memory system integration into agent reasoning loops.

hyperedges.label: Language World Model Training Pipeline
hyperedges.rationale: Five components form integrated training pipeline: data collection feeds three training stages with specific objectives (inject, activate, sharpen) producing language world models.

hyperedges.label: AgentWorldBench Evaluation Framework
hyperedges.rationale: Five components form comprehensive evaluation framework: rubric dimensions, reference-grounded protocol, domain customization, and calibration method enable consistent cross-judge assessment of world model fidelity.

hyperedges.label: World Model Application Paradigms
hyperedges.rationale: Two complementary paradigms (decoupled simulator, unified agent) with three enabling capabilities (scalability, controllability, foundation training) form complete application framework for world models.

hyperedges.label: Agent Infrastructure Ecosystem: World Models + Memory Systems
hyperedges.rationale: Together these concepts form a coherent infrastructure layer for autonomous agents: world models simulate environment dynamics, memory systems persist and retrieve agent state, unified architectures integrate both for improved reasoning and planning.

hyperedges.label: Sim RL Training Paradigm: Simulation + Controllability + Agent Learning
hyperedges.rationale: Sim RL unifies three components: (1) LWM generates simulated environments, (2) controllable simulation injects targeted perturbations, (3) agent RL learns from simulated trajectories, enabling both decoupled and unified training paradigms.
